item.title: Japan weighs phasing out gasoline subsidies from December as costs mount, officials say
item.description: Japan's government is considering scaling back gasoline subsidies from as early as December amid growing concerns that funding for the costly measure could eventually run short, two ruling party officials familiar with the matter said on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Tamiyuki Kihara
item.content:encoded: Japan's government is considering scaling back gasoline subsidies from as early as December amid growing concerns that funding for the costly measure could eventually run short, two ruling party officials familiar with the matter said on Friday. The emergency measure was introduced in March to cushion households and businesses from a surge in oil prices following the start of the US-Israeli war with Iran. As crude oil prices remain elevated, the measure is costing the government several billion dollars a month to keep the nationwide average price of regular gasoline at about 170 yen ($1.09) per litre, rapidly depleting the 3.1 trillion yen [USN:L1N42206P TEXT:"supplementary budget"] approved in June. Under a proposal being discussed by the government and ruling coalition, weekly subsidies paid to fuel distributors could be gradually reduced, pushing average retail gasoline prices to around 175 yen per litre in December and 180 yen in January, the officials said. They declined to be identified as the matter is still private. The Agency for Natural Resources and Energy did not immediately comment. The debate also comes ahead of Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's planned reduction in the consumption tax on food and beverages from April next year. "Once the consumption tax cut begins, households will feel less financial pressure. We would like to reduce gasoline subsidies as much as possible by then," one of the sources said. Japan's government has begun considering other measures to shield households from rising energy costs, including the possible re-introduction of [USN:L4N4680IF TEXT:"gas and electricity subsidies"] that expired in September. ($1 = 156.4800 yen)

item.title: US bans BYD from air base in Japan over security concern, news report says
item.description: The US armed forces have banned Chinese carmaker BYD's EVs from an air base in Japan due to security concerns, South Korea's Yonhap news reported on Friday, after Washington put the company on a list of enterprises it believes are aiding China's military.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The US armed forces have banned Chinese carmaker BYD's (002594.SZ) EVs from an air base in Japan due to security concerns, South Korea's Yonhap news reported on Friday, after Washington put the company on a list of enterprises it believes are aiding China's military. The following are details of the measure. The concern stems from the use of cameras and sensors mounted on the vehicles that the US believes could collect and leak sensitive security related information from the base, Yonhap said, citing US military officials stationed in Japan. US military officials in Japan could not immediately be reached for confirmation. BYD did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The Kadena Air Base in Okinawa will turn around BYD cars starting on Monday, Yonhap said. Vehicles used by base personnel, contractors, commercial entities and taxis will be affected without exception, Yonhap said. In June, the US added BYD along with e-commerce company Alibaba (9988.HK) , internet company Baidu (9888.HK) and automaker NIO (9866.HK) to a [USN:L1N42G0PJ TEXT:"list of companies"] it believes are aiding China's military. [USN:L1N42V0RB TEXT:"Alibaba"] has since sued the US government. China's foreign ministry has protested the list was discriminatory and unreasonable.

item.title: Hall of Famer Marshall Faulk reveals Parkinson's diagnosis
item.description: Pro Football Hall of Famer and Southern University coach Marshall Faulk revealed that he was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease and has been managing the condition for approximately 18 months.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Pro Football Hall of Famer and Southern University coach Marshall Faulk revealed that he was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease and has been managing the condition for approximately 18 months. Faulk, 53, discussed the diagnosis on an episode of "The Caring Neurologist" with Dr. Sandeep Thakkar released Wednesday. The former NFL running back said he initially noticed stiffness in his hand while golfing. When the symptoms persisted during noncompetitive rounds, Faulk brought them up with his doctor during a routine physical and was advised to undergo further testing. Faulk said medication has helped manage his symptoms and allowed him to maintain his normal daily activities. "I just think I caught it early. I'm in a good place," Faulk said. He said he still has occasional tremors and pays close attention to his balance and gait while exercising, but he has remained active since starting treatment. Faulk also encouraged others to have possible symptoms evaluated rather than waiting for them to worsen. Southern hired Faulk as its head coach last November after he spent one season as Colorado's running backs coach. A three-time All-American at San Diego State, he was inducted into the College Football Hall of Fame in 2017. Faulk spent 12 NFL seasons with the Indianapolis Colts and St. Louis Rams after being selected second overall in the 1994 draft. He was honored as the NFL's Most Valuable Player in 2000, earned seven Pro Bowl selections and helped the Rams win Super Bowl XXXIV. He retired with 12,279 rushing yards, 6,875 receiving yards and 136 total touchdowns and was inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 2011. In a statement Thursday, Faulk said he hoped sharing his diagnosis would encourage others to prioritize their health. "This is bigger than football. It is about our health, our families and our future," Faulk wrote. --Field Level Media

item.title: US tariff war is fueling Vietnam's coal boom
item.description: A years-long trade war between the United States and China has helped shift manufacturing investment, factory output and export production into Vietnam, driving the Southeast Asian nation's coal-fired electricity generation to record highs.
item.dc:creator: Gavin Maguire
item.content:encoded: A years-long trade war between the United States and China has helped shift manufacturing investment, factory output and export production into Vietnam, driving the Southeast Asian nation's coal-fired electricity generation to record highs. Vietnam's coal plants generated 132.9 terawatt hours (TWh) of electricity during the first nine months of 2026, which is a 15% jump from the same months last year and the highest for that period on record, according to data from Ember. A roughly 12% decline in year-to-date hydro power production due to below-normal rainfall this summer has been a key driver of the greater coal-fired activity, forcing utilities to offset stunted reservoir output with higher coal production. But a larger factor has been the steady swell in Vietnam's export-oriented manufacturing sector, which has grown rapidly within the past decade and lifted the country's total electricity demand by nearly 50% since 2019. In many respects, that manufacturing expansion can be traced back to Washington. US tariffs on Chinese imports since 2018 encouraged manufacturers to diversify production into lower-cost locations, with Vietnam emerging as one of the biggest winners. The shift has helped supercharge Vietnam's factory sector and power demand, but it has also tied an increasing volume of export production destined for the US market to a power system that still relies heavily on coal for electricity generation. AMERICA'S FACTORY FLOOR The switch in production origins shows up clearly in US trade data. In 2018, US imports from China were roughly 10 times larger than imports from Vietnam. This year, monthly imports from the two countries have been nearly level. When US imports from China hit their peak of roughly $539 billion, average monthly US trade flows to China were around $45 billion, data from LSEG shows. During that same year, average US monthly trade flows to Vietnam were around $4 billion. So far in 2026, average monthly US trade flows to China and Vietnam have been around $22.9 billion and $22 billion, respectively. That more than 400% rise in the value of Vietnam's monthly exports to the US helped fuel an economy-wide boom, with Vietnam's gross domestic product (GDP) posting an average annual expansion of 7.4% since 2022, according to the International Monetary Fund. That growth pace was one of the world's fastest during that period, and in turn triggered sustained growth in Vietnam's total electricity consumption, which expanded at an average rate of 6% a year between 2022 and 2025, data from Ember shows. COAL-HEAVY POWER MIX Vietnam's electricity system is heavily reliant on coal, with coal-fired power stations accounting for an average of around 49% of total utility supplies since 2019. By comparison, coal accounts for around a third of electricity generation globally, which means that Vietnam has a substantially more coal-dependent power system than most. However, coal's share of Vietnam's power mix can fluctuate significantly depending on the availability of alternative power sources in any given year. For instance, coal only accounted for 38.5% of the power mix in 2022 thanks to strong hydro production that year as well as a surge in international coal prices, which spurred nearly all cost-sensitive power systems to pare back coal use. So far in 2026, coal's share has averaged nearly 52% of the generation mix due to the lowest hydro production tally since 2023. That coal share is the highest for that period since 2020, and has resulted in a 16% jump in power sector emissions to a record 129 million metric tons of carbon dioxide and equivalent gases so far this year, data from Ember shows. And with the peak hydro production period already passed, additional gains in both coal use and coal emissions are likely, which will help cement 2026 as a record for Vietnam's coal power reliance. Over the longer term, Vietnam does have significant non-coal power capacity under construction, including around 11 gigawatts (GW) of gas-fired power, 1.4 GW of new hydro capacity, and around 1.3 GW of wind capacity, according to Global Energy Monitor. But there are also an additional 2.7 GW of new coal plants being built, with a further 2.6 GW planned after that. That means that, having won a growing share of the US import demand, Vietnam looks set to primarily power that production with coal. That in turn may serve to keep the cost of goods production relatively low, but comes with its own climate price tag that US importers may have to wrestle with as and when their supply chains come under scrutiny. item.title: Oil little changed as supply concern lingers amid Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia
item.description: Oil prices were little changed in early Asian trade on Friday, after rising 4% to a five-month high in the previous session due to concern of further energy supply disruption after Houthi attacks on top exporter Saudi Arabia.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Oil prices were little changed in early Asian trade on Friday, after rising 4% to a five-month high in the previous session due to concern of further energy supply disruption after Houthi attacks on top exporter Saudi Arabia. Brent crude futures was down 21 cents, or 0.2%, at $112.96 a barrel as of 0030 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate crude was down 27 cents, or 0.3%, at $98.12. On a weekly basis, WTI was on track to end two weeks of gain to finish lower. Brent, which settled at its highest since May 4 on Thursday, is set to close higher for the third successive week. Saudi Aramco (2223.SE) on Thursday [USN:L1N46809Q TEXT:"ordered the evacuation"] of its headquarters in Dhahran on the Gulf near Bahrain, Reuters reported, as fighting intensified between the world's largest crude exporter and Yemen-based Houthis. Clashes between the Houthis and a Saudi-led coalition that backs Yemen's internationally recognised government have raged since the Iran-aligned Houthis pushed towards Bab el-Mandeb, a shipping chokepoint at the mouth of the Red Sea. In Libya, an oil pipeline valve from the Hamada and Tahara oilfields to Zawiya port has been shut, leading to a reduction in production at both fields, the head of the National Oil Corporation told Reuters on Thursday. Separately, Russia said on Wednesday it was ready to resume US-mediated talks with Ukraine next month, after President Vladimir Putin hosted US envoy Steve Witkoff for talks in St Petersburg. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said he hoped negotiations, which would be the first since February, will take place early in November. Russia was the world's third-biggest crude oil producer behind the US and Saudi Arabia in 2025, US energy data showed. Sanctions aimed at keeping Russian energy out of global markets after Russia's invasion of Ukraine in 2022 have pushed up oil prices.

item.title: HD Hyundai to build US shipyard with Kiewit, create 3,000 jobs
item.description: HD Hyundai Co said on Friday it has signed a deal with Kiewit Corp to start building an advanced US shipyard next year, with operations expected to begin in 2029 and create about 3,000 domestic jobs.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: HD Hyundai Co (267250.KS) said on Friday it has signed a deal with Kiewit Corp to start building an advanced US shipyard next year, with operations expected to begin in 2029 and create about 3,000 domestic jobs. The new shipyard is expected to boost US shipbuilding capacity and help revive the industry, Hyundai said. The partners will explore opportunities in both commercial ships and military support vessels, it said in a statement. South Korea pledged to invest $150 billion in the US shipbuilding sector, as part of $350 billion of investment funds the Asian country agreed to put into US projects in return for winning [USN:L6N3TR12K TEXT:"U.S. tariff cuts"] in last year. Construction of the shipyard will begin in 2027 and the two companies will also set up a joint venture. The joint venture will explore building US navy support vessels, commercial ship opportunities, and supplying ship blocks and modules to US shipyards. HD Hyundai said the new shipyard is expected to revive the US shipbuilding industry and expand Korea-US shipbuilding cooperation.

item.title: Australian TV reporter recalls 'terrifying' rescue of man from sinking car
item.description: An Australian television reporter who rescued a man from a car as it was engulfed by floodwaters said on Friday it was terrifying to watch someone almost drown but added "there are few better feelings" than saving a person's life.
item.dc:creator: Stefica Bikesh
item.content:encoded: An Australian television reporter who rescued a man from a car as it was engulfed by floodwaters said on Friday it was terrifying to watch someone almost drown but added "there are few better feelings" than saving a person's life. Will Murray, a journalist with public broadcaster the Australian Broadcasting Corporation, was reporting on flooding north of the city of Brisbane in Queensland state on Thursday, when a man drove a four-wheel drive through floodwater. It then stalled and started to sink. "It was terrifying. Like, the thought of watching someone drown was just, you know, I can see why people would sort of freeze up, because it is just horrifying to watch someone in distress like that," Murray told Reuters. Murray and bystander Daniel Hainey swam out to the car and pulled the driver from the vehicle, moments before it was completely submerged. Murray didn't get the survivor's name or number, but said he hoped the man was doing well. "You know, we had a big old hug after we got him out, and that was just one of the best moments of my life, I have to say, just the relief of seeing him safe and well. That was enough for me," Murray said. Emergency services in south-east Queensland responded to hundreds of distress calls on Thursday and Friday after more than 200 mm (7.9 inches) of rain caused flash flooding that closed roads and schools.

item.title: Rays making calculated gamble in delaying ace to begin World Series
item.description: MILWAUKEE -- Drew Rasmussen has been the epitome of an ace for the Tampa Bay Rays this postseason.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: MILWAUKEE -- Drew Rasmussen has been the epitome of an ace for the Tampa Bay Rays this postseason. In three playoff starts, the right-hander is 2-0 with a 1.29 ERA, allowing three runs over 21 innings, striking out 23 and walking three. After he last pitched in Game 5 of the American League Championship Series, a 3-1 Rays win on Oct. 18, he could have started Game 1 of the World Series against the Milwaukee Brewers on Friday night on normal rest. Tampa, though, is electing to get him an extra day of rest and throw off, instead giving the ball to veteran right-hander Nick Martinez for the opener of the best-of-seven series. "We prioritized Drew getting an extra day. He's had a pretty thick workload here," Rays manager Kevin Cash said Thursday during media day in defense of the decision. "We've relied on him heavily. We know when he takes the ball, we're trying to get the full pitch allotment out of him. "When Nick pitches, we win. So excited to hand Nick the ball (for) Game 1, and we'll go from there." There's not much of a drop-off in terms of the quality Martinez provided this season relative to Rasmussen. He threw a team-high 180 innings this regular season with a 3.10 ERA, trailing only Rasmussen (2.67) among starters. It's quite a come-up for a pitcher who signed a one-year contract with the Rays back in February. "I'm sure you guys can remember my Spring Training wasn't a great one. Now we're here," Martinez said. "Again, I think that speaks a lot about the type of people I have around me to kind of navigate this season and help me out and help me be in this situation, and we're having a lot of fun with it." Martinez is 1-0 with a 3.00 ERA in two starts this postseason. Those starts, though, have lasted a combined nine innings, which may be another factor in starting him Friday when the bullpen is at its freshest. It always helps to have the fresher bullpen in theory, but I love the way Nick has competed," Cash said. "I'm confident and trust that Nick is going to go and find a way to navigate through that lineup a couple times." Another impact of this decision is that it moves Freddy Peralta back to being Tampa's Game 3 starter. While Cash provided a different reason for the choice, it prevents Peralta from the pressure of starting a World Series game in the stadium where he played his first eight major league seasons with the Brewers. "Freddy's workload in the CS was unique in that we did ask him to come out of the bullpen for an inning in between starts and felt like how much of a toll does that take? I don't know," Cash said. "I thought he threw a really good ballgame in Game 6, but I did think towards the end of that game, the velocities and stuff remained the same, the command took a little bit of a dip. Peralta was 70-42 with a 3.59 ERA over 211 games (162 starts) with Milwaukee before he was traded to the New York Mets in January. He struggled in New York but was shipped to Tampa ahead of the trade deadline and responded with a 3.25 ERA in 10 regular-season starts and a 1.08 ERA across four postseason appearances (three starts) for the Rays. He was named ALCS MVP after allowing one run on nine hits over 12 innings across three outings (two starts) against the Guardians. "Getting to manage him, him walking in the door, I got a phone call from Willy Adames saying you're getting one of the best guys in baseball. Come in here, he's got a smile from ear to ear on his face," Cash said. "I give Freddy a lot of credit for being a good pitcher and being vulnerable enough to say I wasn't comfortable doing some things, and I want to get back to my strengths. He guided that through the entire two months he's been with us, and he took off in September and has continued to take off in October." --Field Level Media

item.title: Microsoft develops AI tool that can diagnose 'sequentially' like a doctor
item.description: Microsoft researchers say an AI tool that diagnoses patients step by step, as doctors do, was more than twice as accurate as general physicians at solving complex medical cases, according to a study published on Thursday in Science.
item.dc:creator: Nancy Lapid
item.content:encoded: Microsoft (MSFT.O) researchers say an AI tool that diagnoses patients step by step, as doctors do, was more than twice as accurate as general physicians at solving complex medical cases, according to a study published on Thursday in Science . The model identifies and coordinates the questions that should be asked of a patient, as well as the exams and tests that should be ordered, using an "orchestrator" that organizes how AI will tackle a problem by employing a simulated panel of clinical experts collaborating to solve diagnostic cases, according to the report. Existing medical AI models typically take an all-at-once approach that examines all of a patient's symptoms, lab results and imaging studies to generate a diagnosis. With the orchestrator coordinating the steps to reaching a diagnosis, the AI model first decides what to ask about the patient’s history and what is significant in the physical exam. Based on what it learns, it decides which tests to order, considers the results, and orders further testing as appropriate. All the while, it is updating its working hypotheses and plans, the research leaders said in an interview. Tasked with diagnosing more than 300 highly unusual and confusing medical dilemmas, the model employing the diagnostic orchestrator was more than twice as accurate at "working up" the patient and determining the diagnosis as general physicians using textbooks and the internet. The tool also outperformed human physicians when presented with scenarios drawn from a major database of emergency room admissions. Assessments comparing these types of older systems to human doctors usually use multiple-choice questions, the researchers said. "AI has become very good at getting a 100% pass rate on those,” said Dr. Dominic King, the corporate vice president of the health unit at Microsoft AI, whose team is developing the new technology. “But of course, that's not real-world. No patient ever came to see me with a nice summary.” The researchers also found that diagnostic processes cost less when the orchestrator designs the work-ups than when human doctors do. “We're not just measuring the accuracy of the systems. We're also measuring how judiciously and carefully it goes through a diagnostic work-up,” said Harsha Nori, head of AI at Microsoft AI Health. In a collaboration with Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center in Boston, the researchers will next test the tool’s ability to triage patients in emergency department waiting rooms.

item.title: Japan manufacturing growth slows to 7-month low in October, PMI shows
item.description: Japan's manufacturing sector expanded at its slowest pace in seven months in October as output and new order growth eased, a business survey showed on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Japan's manufacturing sector expanded at its slowest pace in seven months in October as output and new order growth eased, a business survey showed on Friday. The flash S&P Global Japan Manufacturing Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) fell to 53.3 in October from 54.1 in September. A reading above 50.0 indicates expansion in activity, while below that level signals contraction New orders of goods producers rose at the weakest pace since March, while new export business across Japan's private sector increased at the softest rate in four months Manufacturers logged the weakest rise in output since March, while goods producers recorded the slowest increase in new orders since March, the survey showed Factory employment rose at a moderate pace in October. Manufacturers also increased purchasing activity, leading to the largest accumulation in stocks of purchases in almost four years. Service activity edged higher in October. The flash S&P Global Japan Services PMI Business Activity Index rose to 52.0 from 51.3, with the survey showing a stronger increase in business activity and faster sales growth At the broader economy level, the S&P Global Flash Japan Composite PMI Output Index was unchanged at 52.3, marking a 19th straight month of expansion in private sector activity "The October flash PMI data indicated that overall business activity growth across Japan was unchanged from a month prior to remain weaker than the average for the year-to-date," said Usamah Bhatti, economist at S&P Global Market Intelligence Across the private sector, new business rose at the slowest pace in three months and export business growth eased to a four-month low. Job creation slowed to a 14-month low, while confidence for the year ahead weakened to its lowest since July Input cost inflation accelerated slightly in October, driven by higher raw material and labour costs. Firms continued to raise selling prices, although output charge inflation eased to a four-month low

item.title: Trump ally Lewandowski faces criminal investigation over DHS tenure, sources say
item.description: Corey Lewandowski, a former political adviser to President Donald Trump and top aide at the Department of Homeland Security, is under criminal investigation over allegations he profited off his role in the US government, three US officials and a fourth person familiar with the matter told Reuters on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Jana Winter, Andrew Goudsward
item.content:encoded: Corey Lewandowski, a former political adviser to President Donald Trump and top aide at the Department of Homeland Security, is under criminal investigation over allegations he profited off his role in the US government, three US officials and a fourth person familiar with the matter told Reuters on Thursday. The probe began with a criminal referral to the Justice Department from the internal watchdog at DHS, according to the four people. The DHS Inspector General's Office has been investigating Lewandowski's involvement in the handling of certain government contracts, according to one of the people, a DHS official. A lawyer for Lewandowski, Adam Trigg, did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The investigation was first reported in the Wall Street Journal, which quoted Lewandowski's lawyer as saying that his client denies all allegations of wrongdoing. DOJ has not yet issued subpoenas or other legal demands in the criminal investigation, according to one of the people. All four of the people spoke on the condition of anonymity. The Justice Department under Trump has investigated several prominent critics of the president, including former FBI Director James Comey and New York Attorney General Letitia James, but investigations of people close to Trump have been rare. The department has also moved to dismiss several existing cases involving Trump allies, including supporters charged in connection with the January 6, 2021, attack on the Capitol. Asked about media reports on the investigation, Trump told reporters that he did not know the specifics of the investigation, but said, "I want my people to be honest." "And if they're not honest, I'll have my DOJ go and do whatever they have to do," Trump added. Lewandowski served as a top aide to former Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem during her tenure leading DHS. Trump fired Noem in March after months of controversy, including the fatal shootings of two US citizens by federal officers in Minneapolis and lawmakers' questions over a $220 million advertising contract promoting Noem that was awarded without a standard bidding process. Lewandowski had signed some DHS contracts despite having questionable legal authority as a special government employee, according to the DHS official. Certain grants and contracts, including those involving the Federal Emergency Management Agency, were put on hold at Lewandowski's direction, according to two of the people, both of whom are DHS officials. Lewandowski previously served as a campaign manager during Trump's first presidential run in 2016 and advised his 2024 campaign.

item.title: Australia's Zip tumbles 50% after fraud incident dents first-quarter customer growth
item.description: Australia's Zip Co said on Friday an external fraud incident in the US during its fiscal first quarter temporarily weighed on transaction volumes and new customer growth, sending its shares to their lowest level in more than two years.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Australia's Zip Co (ZIP.AX) said on Friday an external fraud incident in the US during its fiscal first quarter temporarily weighed on transaction volumes and new customer growth, sending its shares to their lowest level in more than two years. Shares of the buy now, pay later firm plunged as much as 50.5% to A$1.025 by 2322 GMT, marking their worst intraday session. The selloff erased about A$1.30 billion ($912.08 million) from Zip's market value in early trade before the shares pared some losses. Analysts at Citi said the incident "raises concerns on Zip's onboarding controls", while Jefferies said investors would need greater clarity on whether the increase in operating expenses would persist and how the company plans to prevent similar incidents in future UBS analysts said a key miss was a sharper-than-expected rise in the net bad debts ratio, which came in at 1.97% against their estimate of 1.8%, partly because the fraud event temporarily slowed growth in total transaction value (TTV) in July and August Zip said it identified and contained an external fraud incident involving coordinated actors opening new accounts using legitimate credentials to execute unpaid transactions The incident affected TTV and new customer growth in July and August and resulted in A$10.1 million of cash operating expenses. Zip said it had notified relevant authorities and lodged an insurance claim Net bad debts were 1.93% of TTV in the quarter ended September 30, with some impact from TTV being temporarily moderated by measures taken to contain the fraud Despite the incident, TTV rose 18% to A$4.6 billion in the quarter, while cash earnings before tax, depreciation and amortisation (EBTDA) increased 3.4% to A$65 million ($1 = 1.4253 Australian dollars)

item.title: Justice Department asks appeals court to intervene in California ballot case
item.description: The US Justice Department asked an appeals court on Thursday to intervene in its lawsuit seeking to temporarily block California from counting more than 20,000 mail-in ballots from voters the Trump administration says are likely not US citizens.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The US Justice Department asked an appeals court on Thursday to intervene in its lawsuit seeking to temporarily block California from counting more than 20,000 mail-in ballots from voters the Trump administration says are likely not US citizens. The Justice Department asked the 9th US Circuit Court of Appeals to get involved before a lower-court judge ruled in the dispute. Justice Department lawyers said the unusual maneuver was necessary because the judge assigned to the case, US District Judge David Carter, had not made a decision by Thursday afternoon, as the department had requested. Carter scheduled a hearing for next week to consider the department's request for an emergency order to block California from counting mail-in ballots from more than 20,000 voters in the November 3 midterm elections until their citizenship status could be verified. The department said it interpreted Carter's lack of ruling as a "constructive denial" of its request. The case is being closely watched as the administration of President Donald Trump seeks to exert greater control over the elections next month that will determine control of Congress. In the US, individual states are in charge of running elections.

item.title: UK gas, power grids ready for winter despite global turmoil, operators say
item.description: Britain should have enough gas and electricity to meet peak demand this winter despite higher energy prices driven by conflict in the Middle East, the country's gas and power system operators said on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Nora Buli
item.content:encoded: Britain should have enough gas and electricity to meet peak demand this winter despite higher energy prices driven by conflict in the Middle East, the country's gas and power system operators said on Friday. National Gas and the National Energy System Operator (NESO), which run Britain's gas and electricity networks, published their annual winter outlooks as energy prices remain elevated. UK front-month gas and power prices have risen about 180% and 120%, respectively, since the start of the Iran war, feeding through to [USN:L8N45M0AY TEXT:"consumer bills."] Gas-fired power plants typically set electricity prices, and so higher gas prices tend to push up power costs. National Gas forecasts peak gas demand of 493 million cubic metres per day this winter, 2% higher than last year, largely due to stronger demand from power stations. Overall gas demand is expected to fall 1%. Peak gas supply capacity is estimated at 592 mcm/day, leaving a buffer of 99 mcm/day. That margin would fall to 18 mcm/day if the largest single part of the transmission system failed, a scenario National Gas said was highly unlikely. The operator said a deal [USN:L6N4680GU TEXT:"approved on Thursday"] to maintain import capacity through the Interconnector pipeline from Belgium had improved its outlook, although Europe's [USN:L8N4560S1 TEXT:"lower-than-normal gas storage levels"] are likely to restrain imports. Disruptions in the global liquefied natural gas (LNG) market could also still affect supplies. "Our analysis shows that Great Britain is expected to have sufficient gas supply capability to meet demand throughout winter 2026/27, even under a range of very unlikely high-stress scenarios," said Glenn Bryn-Jacobsen, National Gas' director of energy systems and resilience. On the power side, NESO expects spare capacity of 5.9 gigawatts above peak demand during a typical cold spell, equivalent to 9.5% of peak demand. The margin is broadly in line with recent winters and wider than during the 2022 energy crisis. Higher peak demand has largely been offset by additional battery storage, gas-fired generation and wind power, NESO said. The margin is also higher than its [USN:L8N42Q1L1 TEXT:"June estimate"] because it now expects more wind generation to be available during peak periods. NESO said some days in December and January could be tight and require routine balancing tools such as electricity margin notices. It stressed that such notices signal a need for additional generation and do not indicate a risk to electricity supplies.

item.title: Japan is not yet officially out of deflation, economy minister says
item.description: Japan has yet to see conditions met for the government to officially declare an end to deflation, Economy Minister Minoru Kiuchi said on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Japan has yet to see conditions met for the government to officially declare an end to deflation, Economy Minister Minoru Kiuchi said on Friday. The government's decision on whether to declare an end to deflation will take into account various factors to ensure Japan will not revert to periods of persistent price falls, Kiuchi told a press conference. Kiuchi made the remarks when asked by reporters about [USN:L4N45S011 TEXT:"media reports"] the Bank of Japan may signal that underlying inflation has roughly hit its 2% target at next week's policy meeting.

item.title: EUA vão reforçar triagem do Ebola com novas declarações dos passageiros aéreos
item.description: O governo dos EUA intensificará as medidas destinadas a impedir a entrada de pessoas expostas ao Ebola, com uma nova exigência para que os passageiros aéreos com destino aos EUA atestem que não estiveram na República Democrática do Congo nos últimos 21 dias, de acordo com um memorando divulgado nesta quinta-feira visto pela Reuters.
item.dc:creator: David Shepardson
item.content:encoded: O governo dos EUA intensificará as medidas destinadas a impedir a entrada de pessoas expostas ao Ebola, com uma nova exigência para que os passageiros aéreos com destino aos EUA atestem que não estiveram na República Democrática do Congo nos últimos 21 dias, de acordo com um memorando divulgado nesta quinta-feira visto pela Reuters. Em maio, o Centro de Controle e Prevenção de Doenças (CDC) dos EUA adotou regras que proíbem a entrada de passageiros de avião que tenham estado na RDC — o epicentro do surto de 2026 — nas três semanas anteriores. As restrições foram estendidas aos cidadãos norte-americanos em julho. A nova ordem do CDC entra em vigor em 3 de novembro e exige que todos os passageiros de voos com destino aos EUA apresentem atestados digitais ou em papel. A “Airlines for America”, que representa a United Airlines (UAL.O) , a American Airlines (AAL.O) , a Southwest Airlines (LUV.N) e a Delta Air Lines (DAL.N) , não se pronunciou imediatamente. O CDC realizará teleconferências informativas com as principais companhias aéreas dos EUA e do exterior na sexta-feira para detalhar como as companhias devem cumprir os novos requisitos. Como parte das medidas contra o Ebola, o CDC também proíbe, desde o início deste ano, a entrada de estrangeiros nos EUA caso tenham estado em Uganda ou no Sudão do Sul nas três semanas anteriores. A cepa Bundibugyo do vírus se espalhou sem ser detectada por meses antes de o surto ser declarado em maio. Ela mata cerca de metade das pessoas infectadas e não possui tratamento ou vacina aprovados. Até o momento, está confirmado que o surto já matou cerca de 4.700 pessoas na África, de acordo com o CDC da África. Até o momento, nenhum caso de Ebola associado a esse surto foi relatado nos Estados Unidos, informou o CDC.

item.title: Pacers host Mavs with Tyrese Haliburton back on home court
item.description: Indianapolis will welcome back Tyrese Haliburton, who helped transform the Indiana Pacers into contenders, while Cooper Flagg will look to continue his emergence for the visiting Dallas Mavericks when the teams square off Friday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Indianapolis will welcome back Tyrese Haliburton, who helped transform the Indiana Pacers into contenders, while Cooper Flagg will look to continue his emergence for the visiting Dallas Mavericks when the teams square off Friday. It will be the first home game in 490 days for Haliburton, who missed all of last season after tearing his right Achilles in Game 7 of the 2025 NBA Finals. In the Pacers' season opener, Haliburton flashed the form that made him a two-time All-Star, scoring 23 points and handing out 12 assists in a 123-120 road victory over the New Orleans Pelicans. After the game, Haliburton acknowledged the emotions surrounding his comeback. "I didn't think I was going to cry," he said. "But there was a moment where it just all hit me." Haliburton's return gives Indiana renewed optimism after the Pacers went 19-63 in his absence last season. Reunited with Pascal Siakam, Haliburton hopes to help Indiana recapture the form that carried them to The Finals two seasons ago. Siakam finished with a game-high 30 points against the Pelicans. "You can't take Pascal Siakam for granted," Indiana coach Rick Carlisle said. "... He's so consistent and makes it look so consistently easy." Carlisle said Quenton Jackson was the "hero of the game" against New Orleans after posting six points, four rebounds and three steals in 16 minutes off the bench. "He earned his way into crunch time," Carlisle said. "That's what we need. We need guys playing their hearts out. Anything less isn't going to get us there." The Mavericks fell 128-110 on the road to the Houston Rockets in their season opener, spoiling Dusty May's debut as Dallas coach. Flagg, however, continued his ascent as a dynamic scorer, pouring in a game-high 32 points. It was the highest-scoring performance by a teenager in an NBA season opener, adding another milestone for the 2025 No. 1 overall pick and reigning NBA Rookie of the Year. Flagg also made 11 of 13 free throw attempts. "That's been a point of emphasis," May said. "When we evaluated ourselves after four (preseason) games, getting to the line wasn't something we did well. We thought (Flagg) was the best way to capitalize on that in the paint." Dallas also welcomed back an All-Star guard from a lengthy injury absence. Kyrie Irving scored 15 points in his first game since tearing his left ACL on March 3, 2025. The Mavericks are still working to unlock their offense with Irving back in the lineup alongside Flagg. "(Irving) is obviously a focal point," May said. "There are going to be puzzles we have to figure out. ... We've got to do a better job and find solutions there." The Mavericks trailed Houston 70-38 at halftime after being outscored 38-12 in the second quarter. Flagg pointed to the team's recurring struggles in those 12 minutes. "The thing for us, all preseason has been second quarters," Flagg said. "We've had bad second quarters going into the half. We have to come out and dig ourselves out of a hole in the third quarter. We have to find a way to combat that and have better second quarters." --Field Level Media

item.title: Putin diz que negociações precisam se concentrar na segurança da Rússia, da Ucrânia e da Europa como um todo
item.description: O presidente russo, Vladimir Putin, afirmou nesta quinta-feira que as futuras negociações para a resolução da guerra na Ucrânia deveriam se concentrar em garantias de segurança para ambos os países e em um quadro geral de segurança em toda a Europa.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O presidente russo, Vladimir Putin, afirmou nesta quinta-feira que as futuras negociações para a resolução da guerra na Ucrânia deveriam se concentrar em garantias de segurança para ambos os países e em um quadro geral de segurança em toda a Europa. Putin, entrevistado pela televisão russa um dia após se reunir com o enviado presidencial dos EUA, Steve Witkoff, confirmou que a Rússia está pronta para retomar as negociações com a Ucrânia, mediadas pelos EUA, no próximo mês. Ele reafirmou a política de longa data do Kremlin de que a Rússia nunca quis iniciar uma guerra, mas enfrentou reações hostis da Ucrânia em questões-chave que preocupam Moscou. As negociações sobre diversos assuntos poderiam levar a um resultado positivo, disse ele, mas a Rússia continuava empenhada em uma solução que pusesse fim ao conflito, em vez de um cessar-fogo de curta duração. “O objetivo dessas negociações será garantir a segurança da Ucrânia e da Rússia após a conclusão de acordos de paz, em sua forma definitiva, e não como resultado de um cessar-fogo temporário por um curto período de tempo. Estamos prontos para retomar esses contatos a fim de alcançar esse objetivo”, disse Putin. O presidente russo disse que Witkoff também enfatizou que as discussões deveriam se estender à “arquitetura da segurança europeia como um todo. E eu concordo com isso também. Bem, vamos ver como as coisas se desenvolvem nos próximos dias.” O presidente ucraniano, Volodymyr Zelenskiy, que se reuniu com Witkoff na Noruega na terça-feira, disse que a Ucrânia está pronta para negociações que provavelmente ocorrerão no início do próximo mês. A Ucrânia, afirmou ele, apoia “quaisquer propostas de cessar-fogo, fim da guerra, cessar-fogo energético, bem como iniciativas humanitárias”. Os esforços liderados pelos Estados Unidos para promover as negociações estagnaram em fevereiro com o início do conflito dos EUA e Israel com o Irã. Muitas das questões relacionadas à guerra na Ucrânia se concentram no território, com a Rússia exigindo que a Ucrânia ceda toda a região de Donbas, no leste do país. Kiev rejeita qualquer ideia de abrir mão dos territórios que atualmente controla. Em seus comentários, Putin disse que qualquer discussão sobre territórios no leste da Ucrânia teria de levar em consideração o que, segundo ele, é o fato de que a região é “historicamente terra russa”. E os moradores da região, disse ele, votaram a favor de fazer parte da Rússia em referendos realizados sete meses após Moscou ter iniciado sua invasão. “Em primeiro lugar, minha posição sobre esse assunto é que esse não é o território deles. É o território da Rússia histórica”, afirmou ele.

item.title: Hadjar riles Leclerc by saying Verstappen would be faster in a Ferrari
item.description: Isack Hadjar riled rival Charles Leclerc by suggesting Ferrari had the fastest car and Red Bull teammate Max Verstappen would have won this month's Singapore Grand Prix by an even greater margin if he had been driving for the Italian team.
item.dc:creator: Alan Baldwin
item.content:encoded: Isack Hadjar riled rival Charles Leclerc by suggesting Ferrari had the fastest car and Red Bull teammate Max Verstappen would have won this month's [USN:L1N45X03I TEXT:"Singapore Grand Prix"] by an even greater margin if he had been driving for the Italian team. Leclerc, who finished second in the race and 7.3 seconds behind four-time Formula One champion Verstappen, dismissed the Frenchman's claims at the US Grand Prix on Thursday. "I think it's nonsense to start saying these kinds of things. Isack has no idea what kind of car we drive, and I have no idea what kind of car he drives," the Monegasque told reporters at Austin's Circuit of the Americas. Hadjar, who finished 10th in Singapore, said the Red Bull car was still very hard to drive even if Verstappen has now won the last two races. "In Malaysia, it (the Red Bull) was dominant, but I don't think in Singapore it was the fastest car. That's what I believe. I think if you put Max in the Ferrari, he would have won the race with more margin. So that's my opinion. In Singapore, I think it (the Ferrari) was the fastest car," he said. McLaren's Oscar Piastri said both rivals were stronger than the reigning champions. "I think it wasn't a surprise that Ferrari were very strong in Singapore. I think on the data analysis, they're always the quickest or joint-quickest or outright quickest in basically every corner this year," the Australian said. "But they lose on all the straights, whether that's from drag or power, I don't know ... but we've expected them (Ferrari) to be the benchmark at other circuits and it's not turned out to be the case. I think they're very strong. I think clearly Red Bull was very strong. Both stronger than us for sure. "I think over the last few weeks Red Bull has definitely become the most consistently quick car. But I think each weekend the challenges are kind of rotating."

item.title: Japan's core inflation exceeds BOJ target, cements near-term rate hike chance
item.description: Japan's core consumer inflation exceeded the central bank's 2% target in September for the first time in nine months, data showed on Friday, a sign of broadening price pressure that cements the case for a near-term interest rate hike.
item.dc:creator: Leika Kihara, Takahiko Wada
item.content:encoded: Japan's core consumer inflation exceeded the central bank's 2% target in September for the first time in nine months, data showed on Friday, a sign of broadening price pressure that cements the case for a near-term interest rate hike. The figures underscored how higher fuel costs from the prolonged Middle East conflict, elevated import prices driven by the weak yen and price pressures from robust AI demand were blunting the impact of government fuel subsidies. Having just raised interest rates last month, the Bank of Japan is set to stand pat on policy next week but may revise up its inflation forecast and signal its readiness to keep pushing up still-low borrowing costs, [USN:L4N4650KC TEXT:"sources have told Reuters"]. "Core inflation is expected to accelerate due to rising energy costs from the Middle East conflict and subsequent second-round effects," said Masato Koike, a senior economist at Sompo Institute Plus. "But with price rises not accelerating sharply, there's little need for a back-to-back rate increase in October," he said, projecting the BOJ's next hike to come in December. The core consumer price index (CPI), which excludes volatile fresh food but includes fuel costs, rose 2.1% in September from a year earlier, data showed, matching a median market forecast and accelerating from a 1.7% rise in August. An index that strips away the effects of both volatile fresh food and fuel, which is closely watched by the BOJ as a better gauge of demand-driven price pressures, rose 2.4% in September from a year earlier after increasing 1.9% in August. In a sign of broadening inflationary pressure, goods prices rose 2.8% year-on-year in September, accelerating from a 2.6% gain in August, the data showed. Services inflation also accelerated to 1.5% in September from 1.2% in the previous month, suggesting firms were passing on higher labour costs from a tight job market. RISK OF HIGHER TERMINAL RATE The data will be among factors the BOJ will scrutinise in producing fresh quarterly growth and price forecasts at next week's two-day policy meeting ending on October 30. [USN:L4N45S011 TEXT:"Sources have told Reuters"] the BOJ may signal that underlying inflation - or the broad price trend stripping away temporary, one-off factors - likely achieved 2%, and stress its focus on anchoring inflation around the target. Governor Kazuo Ueda said [USN:L1N4620G5 TEXT:"last week"] the BOJ won't tolerate any inflation overshoot, signalling resolve to continue raising rates after lifting them to a 31-year high of 1.25% [USN:L1N459138 TEXT:"last month"]. [USN:L1N468046 TEXT:"Recent surveys"] showed few signs past rate hikes were cooling loan demand, suggesting scope for further rate increases and drawing attention to the BOJ's assessment on lending conditions. Many analysts [USN:L4N4650G0 TEXT:"polled by Reuters"] expect the BOJ to raise its policy rate to 1.50% in December, and predict the terminal rate to be around 1.75% or 2%. Marcel Thieliant, head of Asia-Pacific at Capital Economics, projects the BOJ to leave policy steady next week but signal continued concerns about upside risks to inflation. "With little evidence that the tightening delivered so far has slowed the economy, the risks are shifting towards a higher peak in the policy rate than our forecast of 2%," Thieliant said.

item.title: Hamilton says he could keep going now that African race is planned
item.description: Seven-time world champion Lewis Hamilton said a race in Africa was a dream that could keep him going longer in the sport now that Formula One has done a deal with Rwanda for a grand prix in the early 2030s.
item.dc:creator: Alan Baldwin
item.content:encoded: Seven-time world champion Lewis Hamilton said a race in Africa was a dream that could keep him going longer in the sport now that Formula One has [USN:L6N45Z0M6 TEXT:"done a deal with Rwanda"] for a grand prix in the early 2030s. The Ferrari driver will be 42 in January and has a contract for 2027. Fernando Alonso, the oldest active F1 driver, is 45 and recently [USN:L6N45L0PA TEXT:"signed up for another season"] with Aston Martin. "I'm now forced to stay a lot longer because we have a race in Africa, and that's been my dream, to be able to race in Africa," Hamilton said at the US Grand Prix on Thursday in a press conference alongside championship leader Kimi Antonelli. "I have to keep fighting to try and stay fit. If I can still punch out good results over the next year, we'll keep it going." Antonelli, who replaced Hamilton at Mercedes last season and is still only 20 years old, encouraged him: "You got to do at least the first one." Hamilton, the sport's first and only Black champion, has long campaigned for a race in Africa -- a continent that last hosted a race at South Africa's Kyalami circuit in 1993 -- and spoke of his efforts. "Countless meetings with the stakeholders, so many meetings with (F1 CEO) Stefano (Domenicali) at his office in London, but also on race weekends, countless calls: 'What's happening? Where are we going? Who are you meeting with?' "Many meetings with different presidents from different countries. Lots of phone calls with different presidents from different countries within Africa," he recalled. "I think for me, it's a place that deserves to have a grand prix. It's about more than just one country. It's about the continent itself." Hamilton said an African race would make people more aware of the continent, but recognized there were concerns. Human rights campaigners Amnesty International [USN:L6N45Z0SJ TEXT:"recently accused Formula One"] of hollow words and offering Rwanda a "sportswashing prize" -- an accusation leveled at countries perceived to be using sport to improve a tarnished image abroad. "Of course, I don't get to choose where we go. Naturally, there are problems all over the world today, so I've seen many of the stories. But I think we really have to approach it with humility," Hamilton said. "Of course, going there doesn't mean that you neglect the things that are happening there. So hopefully many people start to educate themselves a little bit more about what is happening there and what has happened there for hundreds of years. I hope that does spark the conversation."

item.title: From Canada to Nigeria, a race for more 'defence sovereignty' is on
item.description: By the time Eliot Pence stood down as head of international operations for US autonomous weapons powerhouse Anduril in 2022, the Canadian-born executive had spent most of his working life in a US-dominated defence-tech sector he says he and his countrymen rarely questioned.
item.dc:creator: Peter Apps
item.content:encoded: By the time Eliot Pence stood down as head of international operations for US autonomous weapons powerhouse Anduril in 2022, the Canadian-born executive had spent most of his working life in a US-dominated defence-tech sector he says he and his countrymen rarely questioned. In the aftermath of the COVID-19 pandemic and with geopolitical tensions rising, increasing volumes of investment were flowing to a new generation of weapons such as those that company built. Insofar as most US allies thought about defence technology, the priority was its ability to interface directly with a fast-evolving US military. Fast forward four years, and that priority remains. But nations are pushing harder and faster than at any point in recent history to regain more sovereignty in their systems. What that shift means varies widely from country to country, but it is developing some increasingly universal themes, including reducing dependence on the United States and a search for supply chains less controlled by China. Pence - who last year founded Dominion Dynamics, a Canadian defence technology company working to establish sovereign capability in aerospace, autonomy and command-and-control - is on the advisory committee on Canada-US economic relations . Canada's previous strategy of sourcing more than 70% of its defence technology requirements from United States, now faced the new reality of a US administration that was "sometimes antagonistic, to put it mildly", he said. "Canada is now effectively needing to rebuild its defence industry from scratch," he told this columnist on the sidelines of this month's London Resilience Conference showcasing new defence technology alongside venture capital. VARYING THREATS, VARYING RESPONSES Many US allies have been alarmed by limitations placed on the SpaceX-run Starshield system relied on by Ukraine for drone operations and President Donald Trump's plan to buy Russian diesel and decision to [USN:L1N46808R TEXT:"waive new Russia sanctions"]. Trump says he is acting in the interests of the United States. Meanwhile Norwegian media reported this month that Chinese-built electric vehicles taking part in Norwegian military drills were found to have silently filmed participants, although it was not clear if that was deliberately triggered. Multiple nations are racing to source non-China supplies of batteries, components and essential minerals and chemicals, with Beijing tightening controls of multiple rare earths last year in its trade dispute with Washington. Beijing has choked off [USN:L4N4660FG TEXT:"Japan's supplies of yttrium"]– used in jet engines, semiconductors and defence systems - since a diplomatic row between them last year. While some nations are keeping quiet about any policy and industrial shifts to avoid antagonising Washington or Beijing, others are speaking out. Canada's Prime Minister Mark Carney has been one of the loudest critics of Trump, calling for "middle powers" to do much more to chart their own global course. Dominion Dynamics said it had raised C$169 million ($118 million), mainly from Canadian investors, by June. Its early products include the Echo sonar surveillance system that it says will help Canada and close allies – particularly other Arctic nations – keep track of their increasingly contested waters. Like others in Canada, Pence was keen to stress that this did not mean an end to Canada’s long-running direct collaboration with the US Northern Command. But it meant those in charge in Ottawa would also have sovereign systems on which they could rely. Last month, Carney told the New York Times military planners had now drawn up at least limited plans for what he called the "extreme tail risk" – a financial phrase referring to an unlikely but plausible scenario – for the defence of Canada from hypothetical future American attack. Since returning to office at the start of 2025, Trump has on several occasions questioned Canada's right to exist and suggested it might become the 51st US state, although he has generally ruled out using military force. Even more overt threats against Denmark suggesting Washington [USN:L6N460097 TEXT:"might seize Greenland"], though, have also unnerved US allies. What nations like the Baltics, Nordics and Poland now fear is that as in Ukraine, future US administrations might cut access to US systems and weapons stocks to push governments towards US-brokered deals costing territory or independence. MILITARY INDUSTRY AND POWER ARE SHIFTING FAST Established military players such as France, Britain, Germany and South Korea have tended to prioritise "big ticket" items such as ships, tanks and submarines that bring significant numbers of jobs in often politically contested regions. Increasingly, however, officials and a new generation of defence firms are looking to what has happened in Ukraine and well beyond and have concluded that the focus needs to shift to cheap, mass producible systems for attack and surveillance. The result, some defence insiders say, may be a swift and dramatic shift in the global shape of both military industry and power, including in unexpected places. One of the key sponsors of the Resilience Conference was Nigeria's Terra Industries, now with some 200 staff working in Abuja to deliver a range of drones including the Archer with a 1,000-km (620-mile) range and the Kallon solar-powered sentry tower providing 24-hour AI surveillance. Founder Nathan Nwachuku quit university in the US to found an educational technology startup first, but changed tack after considering the threat to the international order posed by Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. SOVEREIGN COMMAND-AND-CONTROL FACES CHALLENGES What African nations like Nigeria faced was not the risk of traditional invasion, he said, but more subtle yet potentially lethal intervention by militant groups, state-armed gangs, financial interests and major powers including Moscow and Beijing. Critical to stopping that, he said, was using cheap technology to secure borders and essential infrastructure. "Our central intelligence platform carries out large-scale command and control, autonomous mission planning and threat intelligence across infrastructure," Nwachuku said, adding that at present no Chinese or US company could offer African firms or governments anything like that. Crucially, while the company is Nigerian, when it works with other nations – so far primarily Ghana – it bases its servers in that country to maintain effective national sovereign control. In the background, the US military and its global command structures are also often quietly supportive of smaller nations building up capability separate to that Washington provides. Sometimes, such joint working can cement broader relations between specific allies. Britain is working with Norway on warships as is Japan with Australia while Canberra is also building the Ghost Shark underwater drone with US-based Anduril and aerial Ghost Bat with Boeing. Analysts and diplomats say the role of the [USN:L6N460097 TEXT:"fledgling UK-Italy-Japan"] Future Global Combat Air Program in Japan's defence relationship with Europe is seen in Tokyo as being as critical as the aeroplane itself, while fighting in Ukraine continues to draw in more and more defence contractors of almost every size and type keen for lessons to take home. But such partnerships are often fraught. Politico this week reported Germany pulling back from its planned Ghost Bat purchase, while a [USN:L8N42G1I7 TEXT:"Franco-German fighter project collapsed in June"]. At another summit in London this month, the senior British officer building an Allied Underwater Battlespace Mission Network – bringing together multiple systems and sensors from the US, Australia and much of Europe – complained nationally driven experimentation and duplication risked wasting resources. Russian and Chinese commentators have this week suggested Washington's latest schism with Ukraine may be permanent and point to future breaks with other allies. Other nations will surely need to learn to do much more on their own – but it will take making those efforts work seamlessly together to keep already watching potential enemies deterred.

item.title: Taiwan shuts down ahead of Typhoon Champi, hundreds of flights cancelled
item.description: Almost all of Taiwan shut down on Friday ahead of the arrival of Typhoon Champi, which is forecast to bring strong winds and torrential rain, though the storm is weakening and is not expected to make direct landfall on the island.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Almost all of Taiwan shut down on Friday ahead of the arrival of Typhoon Champi, which is forecast to bring strong winds and torrential rain, though the storm is weakening and is not expected to make direct landfall on the island. At one point a super typhoon and one of the strongest storms in the Pacific this year, Champi was still packing gusts of around 191 kph (119 mph) near its centre, according to Taiwan's Central Weather Administration (CWA). The storm was about 330 km (205 miles) east of Taiwan's southern tip, the CWA said. The storm's forecast track shows it will pass just off northeastern Taiwan, turn north toward the Chinese coast and eventually move into southern Japan. The administration said its radius was around 320 km (200 miles), large enough to cover most of Taiwan, and weather experts said its impact could last nearly two days. Taiwan's financial markets (.TWII) , will also close for Friday, while only the Taiwan-controlled Kinmen islands, which sit next to the Chinese coast, will open schools and offices as normal. The transport ministry said all 262 domestic flights were cancelled for Friday, along with more than 350 international ones. In the capital Taipei there were squally showers, but public transport including the subway was operating as usual, albeit with reduced service. Taiwan is generally very well prepared for typhoons, which keeps casualties low. Although more common in summer, the storms can strike in autumn too. The typhoon is forecast to first pass over Japan's westernmost inhabited island, Yonaguni, in Okinawa Prefecture.

item.title: LeBron James, 76ers ready for home opener despite 'outside noise'
item.description: PHILADELPHIA -- The Eagles were sent scrambling when blood clots sidelined Jalen Hurts, likely for the year. The Flyers opened their season with nine losses in a row.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: PHILADELPHIA -- The Eagles were sent scrambling when blood clots sidelined Jalen Hurts, likely for the year. The Flyers opened their season with nine losses in a row. Now, with an all-time great on the premises, the stage is set for Philadelphia to be a 76ers city. Three months after LeBron James revealed his fourth team and self-proclaimed "last decision," thousands of fans poured in Thursday to witness James' first home opener with Philadelphia. The crowd bellowed when James was announced in pregame introductions, just before franchise centerpiece Joel Embiid, and he followed his teammates onto the court. Soon after, fans found another level when James performed his ritual "chalk toss" on the scorer's table for the first time in his new home. "Obviously it's always great for the city and the energy," 76ers coach Nick Nurse said pregame. "You can feel it in the streets and stuff and around the building." The Sixers, whose last championship came in 1983, opened the season Tuesday by spoiling the New York Knicks' banner-raising at Madison Square Garden with a 106-100 victory. James compiled 14 points, nine rebounds and seven assists in his team debut. Two days later, James arrived at Xfinity Mobile Arena to face the Cleveland Cavaliers, his hometown team and the franchise he'll be associated with first and foremost. An hour and change before tipoff, James, 41, was on the court warming up wearing a short-sleeved hoodie. Elsewhere, 76ers fans filled the stadium concourse, where jerseys with James' No. 23 and the block-lettered PHILA outnumbered jerseys of Embiid, Jaylen Brown and Tyrese Maxey, the team's other stars. Every seat in the arena bore a free white T-shirt commemorating the Sixers' opening night, with caricatures of Nurse and each player, and James near the center. And legendary Philly boxer Bernard Hopkins was on hand to perform the team's pregame "Ring the Bell" custom, ringing a replica of the Liberty Bell. James, who didn't speak before the game, said at the team's preseason media day that he respected Philadelphia basketball culture, from the famed Palestra gymnasium to his experiences as a visiting player. "It's been like, ‘OK, we respect the way you play the game because we know the game, and we know the history of the game and we've seen so many players play the game. But we hate you. You're not with us, we hate you,'" James explained then. "... And I love that. Actually, I really love it. I really thrive under that circumstance. But yeah, it's always been mutual respect, it's always been mutual respect with myself and the Philly fans." Some additional fuel was added to the fire Thursday when, hours before the game, President Donald Trump wrote on his social media platform that James "disrespect(ed) our country" by appearing to mime a golf swing and a jump shot during the pregame performance of the national anthem Tuesday in New York. "I said right from the beginning that he's no good, a TOTAL DISGRACE," Trump wrote. "LeBron James should apologize to all of those Great American Warriors and Heroes who died for the American Flag, and all that our Country stands for!" Nurse was asked pregame how he felt about that extra layer of outside noise, at the start of the 76ers' most anticipated season in recent memory. "I think that goes right in with other outside noise we've already had, right?" Nurse said. "And I kind of keep saying the same thing. All I really care about is getting them to the practice floor, getting them in the film room, getting them to the game floor, and the focus that they've had and the intent and all the stuff they've had has been excellent." During Thursday's rendition of the anthem by Boyz II Men, James appeared to shift in place to stay loose but did not move more than that. --Adam Zielonka, Field Level Media

item.title: SpaceX seeks access to 80,000 US cell sites for wireless network, Bloomberg News reports
item.description: SpaceX is in talks with cellular infrastructure companies to secure access to at least 80,000 sites across the United States, Bloomberg News reported on Thursday, citing people familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: SpaceX is in talks with cellular infrastructure companies to secure access to at least 80,000 sites across the United States, Bloomberg News reported on Thursday, citing people familiar with the matter. The agreements would potentially solidify the company's path toward building a fourth nationwide wireless carrier. SpaceX, which [USN:L6N45U1AK TEXT:"is buying"] nationwide low-band spectrum, is in talks with mobile infrastructure provider Crown Castle (CCI.N) , according to the report TD Cowen estimated a nationwide terrestrial network would cost more than $80 billion, requiring many years and billions in additional [USN:L4N45V0SC TEXT:"spending"] The 80,000 sites would equal half the 158,500 purpose-built cell towers operational in the US last year, according to the Wireless Infrastructure Association Crown Castle operates about 40,000 US cell towers, while American Tower (AMT.N) has about 42,000 US sites; privately held Vertical Bridge owns around 18,000 Crown Castle CEO Christian Hillabrant said on Wednesday it was talking to "all parties", when asked about potential leases with SpaceX and Amazon (AMZN.O) , but declined to discuss specific customers Crown Castle, American Tower, Vertical Bridge and SpaceX did not immediately respond to Reuters requests for comment Shares of wireless carriers AT&T (T.N) , Verizon (VZ.N) and T-Mobile (TMUS.O) fell between 4.2% and 5% in extended trading

item.title: Mexico's Bimbo lifts lower end of full-year EBITDA outlook
item.description: Mexico's Grupo Bimbo, among the world's top distributors of baked goods, on Thursday raised the lower end of its adjusted EBITDA margin expansion guidance for the year.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Mexico's Grupo Bimbo, among the world's top distributors of baked goods, on Thursday raised the lower end of its adjusted EBITDA margin expansion guidance for the year. The company raised the lower end of its adjusted EBITDA margin to 85 basis points from 70 basis points, while the upper end remained unchanged at 120 basis points. The company maintained its 2026 net sales guidance for mid-single-digit growth and its capital expenditure forecast of between $1 billion and $1.2 billion, management said during a conference call following its third-quarter results. Looking ahead to 2027, management expects continued benefits from its North America "transformation initiatives," profitable growth in Mexico and improving performance in Latin America, but flagged a more inflationary environment, JPMorgan noted following the call. Net profit in the third quarter rose 22% from a year earlier. CEO Alejandro Rodriguez said the company continued to deliver profitable growth due to its progress in the North America transformation and strong momentum in Mexico.

item.title: Singer Raye wins Mercury Prize for 'This Music May Contain Hope'
item.description: Singer Raye won the Mercury Prize for her second studio album "This Music May Contain Hope" on Thursday, beating the likes of veteran Paul McCartney, rock band Suede and rapper Dave for the British music award.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Singer Raye won the Mercury Prize for her second studio album "This Music May Contain Hope" on Thursday, beating the likes of veteran Paul McCartney, rock band Suede and rapper Dave for the British music award. Judges praised the "scale, structure, ambition and sheer charm" of the 28-year-old chart-topper's 73-minute record, which blends jazz, orchestral pop, funk and other genres. "Hope is a very cheesy word ... but hope is just something that we all need," Raye said while accepting the award at the ceremony held in the northern English city of Newcastle. "Music is medicine, so I just hope as well that message comes across to anyone who needs it." First handed out to rockers Primal Scream in 1992, the annual £25,000 ($33,495) Mercury Prize shortlists 12 albums released by British and Irish acts in the United Kingdom in the past year. It is considered less mainstream than the BRIT Awards, Britain's pop music honours, and is open to all music genres. This year's contenders included McCartney, who was nominated for his album "The Boys of Dungeon Lane", and past winners Suede and Dave, who were shortlisted for their respective records "Antidepressants" and "The Boy Who Played The Harp". The nominees also included singer Olivia Dean for "The Art of Loving", former Little Mix star Jade for "That’s Showbiz Baby!", and producer Nia Archives, who was recognised for "Emotional Junglist". Band Knats, musicians Kojey Radical and Dove Ellis were also in the running for their respective records "A Great Day In Newcastle", "Don't Look Down" and "Blizzard". Florence + the Machine's "Everybody Scream" and "Help (2)", a compilation album by various artists for War Child, completed the list. Rocker Sam Fender won the prize last year for his third album "People Watching". ($1 = £0.7464)

item.title: 'Slow down': Hamilton jokes to champion-in-waiting Antonelli
item.description: Lewis Hamilton had one piece of advice for Kimi Antonelli as the 20-year-old Mercedes driver stands on the verge of becoming Formula One's youngest ever champion: "Slow down!"
item.dc:creator: Alan Baldwin
item.content:encoded: Lewis Hamilton had one piece of advice for Kimi Antonelli as the 20-year-old Mercedes driver stands on the verge of becoming Formula One's youngest ever champion: "Slow down!" The Italian would have to win the US Grand Prix and have everything else fall his way for the title to be secured in Austin on Sunday but, with a lead of 102 points and a maximum 150 still to be won, he can be sure it is just a matter of time. Hamilton, winner of seven championships and the most successful driver in the history of the sport, left no doubt he was joking. "He doesn't need any advice. I think he's shown this year, and also last year, but particularly this year, his talent and his ability, his calmness and his approach," said the Ferrari driver of the man who replaced him at Mercedes last season. "He's done an amazing job this year, and I'm so proud of him. I'm so proud of the way he's carried himself, how he interacts with the drivers and even with you guys," he told reporters on Thursday. "It's great to see him and the team excel. If it's not my team, I'd always want to see my old team do well." Antonelli would be the first Italian to take the title since Alberto Ascari in 1953 and, while professing to be taking one race at a time, he knows what awaits. "It definitely is crazy if you think about it, but that's why I won't think about it," he said of the possibility that he could be champion already on Sunday with five races to spare as the calendar stands. "I've heard that something catastrophic needs to happen to the others for me to become champion (in Austin). For me, it needs to be a perfect weekend. The others need to have a poor result, which is unlikely to happen," he added. Antonelli said following in Hamilton's footsteps as a champion as well as a Mercedes driver would be a dream come true, but also made clear he was prepared to wait. "Obviously, I'm in an incredible position... But, of course, I still have to keep going, and the mindset is always the same: whenever I go on track, I want to be at the top and try to win as much as possible, whether I win the championship this weekend, next weekend or in Brazil. Let's see," he said.

item.title: Deckers results show aggressive discounts from rivals are hitting premium brands
item.description: Deckers Outdoor , the maker of UGG boots and Hoka sneakers, said aggressive discounting by rivals hurt its sales in the second quarter, highlighting challenges facing premium footwear brands as shoppers grow more selective.
item.dc:creator: Sanskriti Shekhar
item.content:encoded: Deckers Outdoor (DECK.N) , the maker of UGG boots and Hoka sneakers, said aggressive discounting by rivals hurt its sales in the second quarter, highlighting challenges facing premium footwear brands as shoppers grow more selective. Shares of the company fell 8% in extended trading after the results. Here are more details: The footwear maker reported sales of $1.48 billion, [USN:L1N46819K TEXT:"missing"] analysts' estimate of $1.51 billion, but reported a 27% rise in profit for the quarter ended September 30 "In the US, we saw promotional activity increase throughout the quarter, particularly in athletic footwear, which weighed on our US e-commerce performance as we maintained full-price discipline," CEO Stefano Caroti said on the company's earnings call Comparable direct-to-consumer sales fell 6.4% in the second quarter "There is a heightened focus on revenues over margins," said Simeon A. Siegel, analyst at CFA "Share declines were evident across every household income bracket, including higher-income consumers, highlighting the challenges facing even premium brands as shoppers become more selective," said Michael Gunther, analyst at Consumer Edge Deckers continues to grapple with intense competition in the athletic footwear market, including from larger rivals such as Nike (NKE.N) "Where we potentially lose share to others are the more compressed price points below $120, where the competition is greater," CEO Caroti said "We will continue to prioritize margin preservation and long-term value over chasing potential incremental near-term revenue that could dilute our brands," he added

item.title: Florida attorney general proposes bill that limits social media, AI features for teens in the state
item.description: Days after Florida lost its bid for a court order forcing Meta Platforms to overhaul Instagram and Facebook for teens in the state, its attorney general said he was proposing legislation that would force the company to make the same changes.
item.dc:creator: Diana Jones
item.content:encoded: Days after Florida lost its bid for a court order forcing Meta Platforms (META.O) to overhaul Instagram and Facebook for teens in the state, its attorney general said he was proposing legislation that would force the company to make the same changes.
